subject: Private observability: egress scaling, SIEM forwarding, and tracing hooks

Subject: Private observability: egress scaling, SIEM forwarding, and tracing hooks

Hi Patrick / Globex security team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As promised, attaching the initial proposal for how Redwood will handle observability export from a private VPC deployment at scale. The three areas we want to lock down before the acceptance test run are:

- Egress throughput and bursting behavior for log/metric export (Splunk HEC + S3-forwarders)
- SIEM integration: batching, envelope format, authentication options (HEC token vs mTLS)
- Tracing hooks: sampling/leakage boundaries and how we expose trace-context for customer collectors

Immediate asks:
1) Confirm acceptable HEC ingestion concurrency and whether you require mTLS on top of HEC tokens.
2) Share any egress firewall/ACL constraints (CIDR allowlists, port ranges).
3) Any retention/arbitration rules (we have a short retry + dead-letter bucket plan).

Attachments: egress_scaling_diagram.png (diagram), splunk_hec_sample.conf (sample config), tracing_hook_spec.pdf (hooks proposal)

I'll coordinate a short design review on Wednesday if that works — propose 30m to walk the diagram and acceptance criteria.

Thanks,

Lauren Bishop
Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Patrick Mullen <patrick.mullen@globex.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: security.ops@globex.com, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T17:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private observability: egress scaling, SIEM forwarding, and tracing hooks

Thanks Lauren — this is helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- HEC vs mTLS: security wants mTLS between our collector and Redwood's forwarder for the on-prem deployment. HEC token alone won't be sufficient for the regulated streams.
- Egress ACLs: we can open a /27 to your forwarder pool; will confirm the exact CIDR by EOD Monday.
- Concurrency: Splunk expects bursts up to ~150 events/sec per host during peak; aggregate for our initial rollout will be ~1.2k eps. Can your batching handle bursts without message reorder?

Acceptance criteria for our audit team: ordered envelopes per host (best-effort), at-least-once delivery with dead-letter placement for persistent failures, and signed manifests for evidence transfer during onboarding. We can make the meeting Wed 10am PT.

—Patrick
Head of Security Integrations
Globex Corporation
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Patrick Mullen <patrick.mullen@globex.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private observability: egress scaling, SIEM forwarding, and tracing hooks

Patrick — great points. Quick technical notes and open questions: 

- mTLS: we support mTLS for forwarder-to-collector connections in Private deployments. For Splunk HEC specifically we can terminate HEC on our side and present mTLS upstream, or we can deliver directly to your Splunk HEC with mTLS + HEC token. Recommendation: direct mTLS to your HEC endpoint to reduce envelope translation.

- Batching and ordering: our forwarder uses host-keyed FIFO queues with sequence numbers in the envelope header. Batching is adaptive: we batch up to 1MB or 2000 events or 500ms whichever comes first. This preserves ordering per host while allowing bursts. For your 1.2k eps target, we recommend a minimum of 4 forwarder instances in the initial pool with autoscale + burst headroom at 8.

- Backpressure and retries: we support backoff + local persistence to a disk-backed queue (encrypted) with a configurable max retention before moving to a dead-letter S3. Retention TTL is configurable per-customer; default 72h.

Open questions for Globex (please confirm):
1) Do you prefer envelope signing (we can sign manifests with an issuing key) or just TLS evidence for audits?
2) Any egress NAT constraints that would force us to use a proxy chain? (We can support proxy with mTLS but need the proxy to forward client certs)

I'll attach a trimmed YAML with recommended forwarder counts and an example Splunk HEC config in our shared drive during the meeting.

Ben Carter
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: splunk_hec_sample.conf (referenced)

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps:

- Meeting confirmed: Wed 2027-04-14 10:00 AM PT (30m) — design walk + acceptance checklist. Invite sent.
- Action items for Globex: supply exact CIDR for allowlist and confirm whether you want envelope signing in addition to mTLS (Patrick).
- Action items for Redwood: Ben will prepare a scaled-forwarder plan (instances, expected per-instance throughput, disk persistence sizing) and a short doc on trace-context propagation and sampling boundaries (Marissa).
- Evidence: we'll produce signed manifests per batch during onboarding and snapshot logs for auditors; Kimberly will own the evidence checklist.

If anything changes before the meeting, ping me. Otherwise we'll use the meeting to lock the YAML config and the acceptance test steps.

Lauren
Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
